A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SURE-VQA. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material and distinguishing changed evaluation settings.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments on three medical VQA datasets, a human-rater study, and corruption and multimodal-shift analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports these empirical studies with revised evaluation and adds LLM-evaluator comparisons, a non-medical base model, alternative held-out splits and statistical analyses.

M1.justification: The framework's evaluator component changes from Mistral to Gemma. Appendix A.2 also revises closed-ended prompts to explicitly accept synonymous answers and additional irrelevant detail. The three requirements, hybrid exact-match/LLM scoring structure and fine-tuning methods remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use English SLAKE, OVQA and MIMIC-CXR-VQA with the same medical VQA coverage. The new swapped-shift study changes which existing SLAKE modalities and question categories are held out, rather than introducing new data or task types. Corruption and combined OVQA shifts already appear in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds LLaVA 1.6 as a non-medical comparator to LLaVA-Med 1.5 throughout the robustness experiments. Appendix B.1 also expands the evaluator comparison beyond Mistral and traditional metrics to models including Phi-3, Gemma, Qwen, LLaMA, Granite, Biomistral and Prometheus. The original fine-tuning and sanity-baseline sets remain.

E3.justification: Evaluation switches from Mistral to Gemma with revised closed-ended grading prompts, and the human study increases from 50 to 100 questions per dataset. New protocols evaluate LLaVA 1.6 and hold out MRI or Position categories in SLAKE instead of X-Ray or Size. Original dataset sizes, preprocessing and hyperparameter-search ranges are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds per-question image/no-image win-tie-loss analysis, comparisons among LLM judges, and a SLAKE ablation testing sensitivity to held-out categories. Appendix C.5.1 adds statistical examinations of robustness rankings and variability. The corruption study and multimodal-shift ablation are retained, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: New Appendix C.5.1 reports 100 bootstrapped robustness estimates per experiment, pairwise Welch tests with multiple-testing correction, and ANOVA F-values and p-values. These substantially extend v1's robustness uncertainty reporting. The existing three-seed PEFT means and standard deviations remain; no increase in training seeds is established.

E6.justification: Tables 14-19 revise scores and add non-medical-model results, alongside new evaluator, swapped-shift and statistical findings. For example, OVQA LoRA's open-ended question-type OoD score changes from 1.72 to 1.98 in Table 16. Because the evaluator changes from Mistral to Gemma, this is a replaced measurement, not a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The relative-robustness definition is unchanged, and neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. The new bootstrap, Welch-test and ANOVA procedures are empirical statistical analyses rather than new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: v2 adds the conclusion that medical and non-medical base models perform similarly after fine-tuning. The three framework requirements, strong language-only baselines, LoRA's in-distribution advantage and absence of a consistent robustness winner remain. Greater abstract emphasis on shift-versus-method variability restates a conclusion already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific qualifications about medical-knowledge and demographic biases in LLM judges, the predominantly radiological scope, and the framework's status as a research tool rather than a clinically deployable benchmark. Appendix E further explains generalization through related question patterns and recommends greater training-data diversity.

D1.justification: v2 supplies separate selected hyperparameters for the non-medical model, revised evaluator prompts, and explicit identification of LLaVA-Med with (IA)3 for the retained multimodal ablation. Dataset-processing instructions and code-access information remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gemma, Bahri et al. and Jeong et al., positioning its fine-tuned medical/non-medical comparison against Jeong's zero- and few-shot findings. Some contextual references, including Yoon et al. and Ma et al., disappear. The central positioning around three evaluation pitfalls remains.

P1.justification: The former framework-setup and separate fine-tuning-study sections become a unified Empirical Study with explicit R1-R3 validation subsections. Results discussion and conclusions are rewritten, and appendix dataset details move before hyperparameter searches. This substantially reorganizes the narrative beyond merely appending experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds win-tie-loss charts, an expanded evaluator heatmap, non-medical-model plots, a significance matrix, a corruption-pipeline diagram and swapped-shift panels. Tables gain medical/non-medical subdivisions, qualitative examples move to the appendix, and the publication template changes typography and page layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation by comparing multiple judges on a larger human-rated sample, checking robustness findings with a second base model, and testing alternative held-out categories. These address v1's dependence on one evaluator and one backbone. Added statistical analyses and explicit applicability limitations improve assessability, although changed scoring prevents interpreting cross-version numerical differences as performance gains.
